questions.question: In the guide's solving algorithm for dice problems, what is the first step after identifying the labels on each given view?
options: Immediately guess the answer from the options
Find any known opposite face pairs across the given views
Assume all dice are numbered identically to a standard die
questions.rationale: The solving flowchart moves from identifying labels straight to finding known opposite-face pairs, since opposite pairs (faces that never appear together in any single view) are the most reliable and reusable deduction.

questions.question: If two faces of a die appear together (both visible) in even one given view, what can you conclude about them?
options: They cannot be opposite faces, since opposite faces never appear together in the same view
They are always adjacent to every other face
questions.rationale: A standard cube's opposite faces are on parallel sides and can never both be visible in the same single view — so two faces seen together in one view rule out the possibility that they are opposite.

questions.question: According to the solving flowchart, when should you reject an answer option?
options: Whenever the option contains an unfamiliar face label
When the option shows a known opposite pair touching/adjacent to each other, which is impossible
Whenever the option shows the die rotated at all
Options should never be rejected before full rotation tracking
questions.rationale: Since opposite faces can never be adjacent on a cube, an answer option depicting a known opposite pair as touching is immediately invalid and can be rejected without needing full rotation tracking.

questions.question: When is tracking the die's exact rotation/orientation necessary, according to the solving method?
options: For every dice question, without exception
Only when the question requires an exact orientation match, not just an adjacency/opposite-rule check
Never — opposite-pair logic alone always suffices
Only when fewer than two views are given
questions.rationale: The flowchart branches: if the question only needs an adjacency/opposite-rule answer, that check is enough; full rotation tracking is only needed when an exact orientation match is required.
